- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
Reading the spec now. It's short on the details that actually drive the architecture, so before sketching a real plan I want to separate what's decidable from what needs your input.

**What's clear from the spec:**
- Users subscribe to alert topics (news, markets, disasters, ...) with some filtering
- Delivery is multi-channel (email + Slack now), and the channel layer needs to be pluggable for future channels
- There's an admin surface, scope unstated

**Rough shape I'd propose** (four building blocks, regardless of the open questions below):
1. **Event ingestion** — pulls/receives raw events from external sources (news API, market data feed, disaster feed like USGS/NOAA) and normalizes them into a common `Event` shape.
2. **Alert matching engine** — evaluates each incoming event against active user `AlertSubscription`s (topic + filters like keywords, tickers, region, magnitude threshold) and produces `AlertMatch`es.
3. **Notification dispatch** — a `NotificationChannel` interface (`send(userChannelConfig, alertMatch)`) with adapters for Email and Slack registered in a channel registry; adding SMS/push/webhook later means writing one new adapter, not touching the matching engine.
4. **Admin view** — management/observability UI over the above (scope TBD, see below).

**Where I can't plan responsibly without your input** — these change the architecture, not just the UI:

content.text: RSS is a solid, low-cost way to bootstrap the *news* category specifically — no API keys, wide outlet coverage, and it fits the "normalize into a common Event shape" ingestion layer we sketched. The catch: it's poll-based (so "near real-time" really means "as fast as your poll interval," typically 1–5 min, not seconds), feeds vary wildly in quality/structure so you'll need dedup and noise-filtering across sources, and it doesn't cover markets or disasters at all — those need dedicated APIs (a market data feed, USGS/NOAA) regardless. I'd treat RSS as one ingestion adapter among several, not the whole strategy.

market movement news should come from here: https://feeds.content.dowjones.io/public/rss/mw_topstories
disaster news should come from here: https://www.nytimes.com/svc/collections/v1/publish/https://www.nytimes.com/topic/organization/federal-emergency-management-agency/rss.xml
and breaking news from here: https://rss.nytimes.com/services/xml/rss/nyt/World.xml
but the structure should support another sources and another formats (like websocket)

Good, that resolves the event-source question. Here's how I'd fold it in:

**Ingestion needs a `Source` adapter, symmetric to the notification `Channel` adapter.** Two source types:
- **Poll sources** (your three RSS feeds): adapter exposes `fetch()`, run on a scheduler per source (e.g. every 1–5 min), diffed against last-seen `guid`/`pubDate` to avoid re-emitting old items.
- **Stream sources** (future websocket): adapter exposes `connect(onEvent)`, holds a persistent connection, emits as items arrive.

Both normalize into the same internal `Event` shape (`sourceId, category, title, summary, url, publishedAt, raw`) and push it through one internal bus. The matching engine only ever reads off that bus — it doesn't know or care whether the event came from RSS polling or a websocket push. Adding a fourth source later (e.g. a market data websocket, or a different disaster API) means writing one adapter, not touching ingestion, matching, or dispatch.

One detail worth deciding now rather than later: `category` (news/markets/disasters) — is it a fixed property of each source (Dow Jones feed is always "markets"), or should a single source be able to emit multiple categories? With your three feeds it's 1:1, so I'd default to fixed-per-source unless you expect mixed-category feeds later.

Still open from before, since they shape the plan materially:
1. Does this extend the current sonrisa2 repo (Node/TS + Angular), or is it a separate service?
2. Admin view — just monitoring (users, subscriptions, delivery logs), or also source/rule management?

it is a 1:1 relation
1, yes it's extend the current sonrisa 2 repo
2, admin view: rss feed crud, user crud, category crud (category is a different table)
also need a database to store older news, users, categories, sources and user subscriptions

Good, that closes out the major architecture decisions. Here's the consolidated plan:

**Data model (Postgres, via Prisma — fits the existing Node/TS backend with type-safe migrations):**
- `categories` (id, name, slug) — admin CRUD
- `sources` (id, name, url, type: `rss`\|`websocket`, category_id FK, poll_interval_seconds, active) — admin CRUD, 1:1 with category as agreed
- `events` (id, source_id FK, external_id/guid, title, summary, url, published_at, ingested_at) — the news archive
- `users` (id, email, name, role, created_at) — admin CRUD
- `user_channels` (id, user_id FK, channel_type: `email`\|`slack`, config JSONB, active) — where each user's email address / Slack webhook lives
- `subscriptions` (id, user_id FK, category_id FK, active) — which categories a user wants alerts for
- `deliveries` (id, subscription_id FK, event_id FK, channel_id FK, status, sent_at) — audit log; also lets us dedupe so a user isn't notified twice for the same event

**Backend modules (all within the existing `backend/` app — no need for a separate service at this scale):**
- `sources/` — `SourceAdapter` interface (`poll` type now: `RssAdapter`; `stream` type later: `WebsocketAdapter`), a scheduler that polls active sources on their configured interval
- `ingestion/` — normalizes fetched items into `Event`, dedupes by `external_id`, persists, publishes to an internal event bus
- `matching/` — listens on the bus, finds active subscriptions for the event's category, produces matches
- `notifications/` — `NotificationChannel` interface (`EmailChannel`, `SlackChannel`), dispatches matches to each user's configured channels, writes `deliveries`
- `admin/` — REST CRUD for sources, categories, users
- `api/` — user-facing endpoints: manage own subscriptions and channel config

For the bus, I'd start with a plain in-process EventEmitter rather than Kafka/Redis — one Node process, moderate polling volume, no need for that complexity yet. Since adapters just emit/consume normalized events, swapping in a real queue later wouldn't touch the adapter code.

**Two things I still need from you before this is buildable:**
1. **Auth on the admin view** — it's CRUD over real user data, so it needs to be gated. Do you already have an auth mechanism in mind (JWT session, SSO, something existing elsewhere), or should I plan a basic login for this?
2. **Subscription granularity** — is "subscribe to a category" (e.g. all Markets news) enough for v1, or do users need finer filters (keywords, tickers, regions) within a category? Affects whether `subscriptions` needs a `filters` JSON column now or can add it later.

So a category's Slack channel gets every news item for that category regardless of subscriber count, while email only reaches people who subscribed. Let me know if that's not what you meant.

**Notification dispatch, updated:**
- `EmailChannel.send(news, user)` — fired once per active subscription match
- `SlackChannel.send(news, category)` — fired once per news item, only if `category.slack_webhook_url` is set

**Phase 0 — Foundation**
1. Add PostgreSQL to `docker-compose.yml`; add Prisma to `backend/`

**Phase 3 — Ingestion**

8. Scheduler that polls active RSS sources on their configured interval
9. Ingestion normalizer: dedupe by `external_id`, persist to `news`, publish to the internal event bus

**Phase 4 — Matching + Notification**

11. `NotificationChannel` interface + `EmailChannel` + `SlackChannel`

**Phase 5 — User-facing API**

**Phase 6 — Frontend (Angular)**
14. Auth screens + JWT interceptor
15. Admin views: categories/sources/users CRUD tables+forms
16. User view: browse categories, subscribe/unsubscribe

**Phase 7 — Verification**
17. End-to-end check via `docker compose up`

Each phase builds on the last (schema → auth → admin CRUD → ingestion → matching/notify → user API → frontend), so I'd execute in this order. Want me to start at step 1, or adjust the breakdown first?

input.content:
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum Role {
  ADMIN
  USER
}

enum SourceType {
  RSS
  WEBSOCKET
}

enum Channel {
  EMAIL
  SLACK
}

enum DeliveryStatus {
  PENDING
  SENT
  FAILED
}

model Category {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  name            String
  slug            String   @unique
  slackWebhookUrl String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  sources       Source[]
  subscriptions Subscription[]
  deliveries    Delivery[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Source {
  id                  String     @id @default(cuid())
  name                String
  url                 String
  type                SourceType @default(RSS)
  pollIntervalSeconds Int        @default(300)
  active              Boolean    @default(true)
  createdAt           DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt           DateTime   @updatedAt

  categoryId String
  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  news News[]

  @@map("sources")
}

model News {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  externalId  String
  title       String
  summary     String?
  url         String
  publishedAt DateTime
  ingestedAt  DateTime @default(now())

  sourceId String
  source   Source @relation(fields: [sourceId], references: [id])

  deliveries Delivery[]

  @@unique([sourceId, externalId])
  @@map("news")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  email        String   @unique
  name         String
  passwordHash String
  role         Role     @default(USER)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  subscriptions Subscription[]
  deliveries    Delivery[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Subscription {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  active     Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())

  userId String
  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  categoryId String
  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  @@unique([userId, categoryId])
  @@map("subscriptions")
}

model Delivery {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  channel   Channel
  status    DeliveryStatus @default(PENDING)
  error     String?
  sentAt    DateTime?
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now())

  newsId String
  news   News   @relation(fields: [newsId], references: [id])

  // Set for EMAIL deliveries (one per subscribed user)
  userId String?
  user   User?   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  // Set for SLACK deliveries (one broadcast per category)
  categoryId String?
  category   Category? @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  @@unique([newsId, channel, userId])
  @@unique([newsId, channel, categoryId])
  @@map("deliveries")
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum Role {
  ADMIN
  USER
}

enum SourceType {
  RSS
  WEBSOCKET
}

enum Channel {
  EMAIL
  SLACK
}

enum DeliveryStatus {
  PENDING
  SENT
  FAILED
}

model Category {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  name            String
  slug            String   @unique
  slackWebhookUrl String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  sources       Source[]
  subscriptions Subscription[]
  deliveries    Delivery[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Source {
  id                  String     @id @default(cuid())
  name                String
  url                 String
  type                SourceType @default(RSS)
  pollIntervalSeconds Int        @default(300)
  active              Boolean    @default(true)
  createdAt           DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt           DateTime   @updatedAt

  categoryId String
  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  news News[]

  @@map("sources")
}

model News {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  externalId  String
  title       String
  summary     String?
  url         String
  publishedAt DateTime
  ingestedAt  DateTime @default(now())

  sourceId String
  source   Source @relation(fields: [sourceId], references: [id])

  deliveries Delivery[]

  @@unique([sourceId, externalId])
  @@map("news")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  email        String   @unique
  name         String
  passwordHash String
  role         Role     @default(USER)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  subscriptions Subscription[]
  deliveries    Delivery[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Subscription {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  active    Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  userId String
  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  categoryId String
  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  @@unique([userId, categoryId])
  @@map("subscriptions")
}

model Delivery {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  channel   Channel
  status    DeliveryStatus @default(PENDING)
  error     String?
  sentAt    DateTime?
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now())

  newsId String
  news   News   @relation(fields: [newsId], references: [id])

  // Set for EMAIL deliveries (one per subscribed user)
  userId String?
  user   User?   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  // Set for SLACK deliveries (one broadcast per category)
  categoryId String?
  category   Category? @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  @@unique([newsId, channel, userId])
  @@unique([newsId, channel, categoryId])
  @@map("deliveries")
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
}

enum Role {
  ADMIN
  USER
}

enum SourceType {
  RSS
  WEBSOCKET
}

enum Channel {
  EMAIL
  SLACK
}

enum DeliveryStatus {
  PENDING
  SENT
  FAILED
}

model Category {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  name            String
  slug            String   @unique
  slackWebhookUrl String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  sources       Source[]
  subscriptions Subscription[]
  deliveries    Delivery[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Source {
  id                  String     @id @default(cuid())
  name                String
  url                 String
  type                SourceType @default(RSS)
  pollIntervalSeconds Int        @default(300)
  active              Boolean    @default(true)
  createdAt           DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt           DateTime   @updatedAt

  categoryId String
  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  news News[]

  @@map("sources")
}

model News {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  externalId  String
  title       String
  summary     String?
  url         String
  publishedAt DateTime
  ingestedAt  DateTime @default(now())

  sourceId String
  source   Source @relation(fields: [sourceId], references: [id])

  deliveries Delivery[]

  @@unique([sourceId, externalId])
  @@map("news")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  email        String   @unique
  name         String
  passwordHash String
  role         Role     @default(USER)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  subscriptions Subscription[]
  deliveries    Delivery[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Subscription {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  active    Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  userId String
  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  categoryId String
  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  @@unique([userId, categoryId])
  @@map("subscriptions")
}

model Delivery {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  channel   Channel
  status    DeliveryStatus @default(PENDING)
  error     String?
  sentAt    DateTime?
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now())

  newsId String
  news   News   @relation(fields: [newsId], references: [id])

  // Set for EMAIL deliveries (one per subscribed user)
  userId String?
  user   User?   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  // Set for SLACK deliveries (one broadcast per category)
  categoryId String?
  category   Category? @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])

  @@unique([newsId, channel, userId])
  @@unique([newsId, channel, categoryId])
  @@map("deliveries")
}

    ports:

    depends_on:

    restart: unless-stopped

content.text: Found a real bug: the backend Docker image sets `NODE_ENV=production`, which flipped the auth cookie to `Secure`. Since this stack is plain HTTP (no TLS termination anywhere), browsers/curl silently refuse to send it back — login "succeeds" but the session cookie never round-trips. `NODE_ENV=production` conflated "production build" with "served over HTTPS," which isn't true here. Decoupling those.

content.text:
Phase 1 done:

- **Auth module** (`backend/src/auth/`): `jwt.ts` (sign/verify), `cookie.ts` (shared httpOnly-cookie config), `middleware.ts` (`requireAuth`, `requireRole`), `routes.ts` (`POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me`).
- Sessions live in an **httpOnly, JWT cookie** (not a bearer token the client manages) — that's what makes `logout` a real action (clearing the cookie) instead of a no-op, since JWTs are otherwise stateless.
- Passwords hashed with `bcryptjs` (pure-JS, avoids native build tooling in the Alpine Docker image).
- `JWT_SECRET` now lives in a root `.env` (gitignored, `.env.example` documents it) and flows into the backend container via `docker-compose.yml`.

**Bug caught during verification**: the backend Dockerfile sets `NODE_ENV=production`, and the cookie's `secure` flag was tied to that — so over plain HTTP (this stack has no TLS anywhere) the browser/curl would silently refuse to send the cookie back, breaking every authenticated request right after a successful login. Fixed by decoupling `secure` from `NODE_ENV` into its own `COOKIE_SECURE` env var (defaults to `false`; flip it on once there's real TLS termination in front of this service).

Verified live against the running containers: register → sets cookie → `/me` authenticates → logout clears cookie → `/me` correctly rejects → login with wrong password correctly rejects.

aiTitle: Create Node.js TypeScript backend with Angular frontend

content.text:
Back to normal. Set up and verified live-reload for the frontend:

- **`frontend/proxy.conf.json`**: routes `/api/*` from the dev server straight to `http://backend:3000` over the Docker network — no need to publish the backend's port to the host.
- **`docker-compose.dev.yml`**: an additive override (doesn't touch `docker-compose.yml`) that swaps the `frontend` service from the nginx production build to `ng serve --host 0.0.0.0` with your source bind-mounted in, `node_modules` kept in its own volume (so the Linux container doesn't inherit your Windows host's `node_modules`), and `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING` enabled since bind-mounted NTFS paths don't always propagate native file-change events reliably into Docker Desktop.

**To use it:**
```
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d frontend
```
This serves the app at **http://localhost:4200** with live reload — I verified a source edit triggered an automatic rebuild in ~0.25s and pushed a component update to the client. Note this *replaces* the frontend container while active, so port 80 goes down until you switch back with:
```
docker compose up -d --build frontend
```
(which I've done — `http://localhost` is back to the normal prod build, confirmed working.)

content.text: Confirmed — this project has no `zone.js` at all (it's not in `angular.json`, `main.ts`, or `package.json`), so it's running Angular's newer zoneless change detection by default. In zoneless mode, only signal writes (or a few other explicit triggers) schedule a re-render; a plain field mutated inside an async `subscribe()` callback — which fires well after the synchronous `submit()` call stack that Angular *did* check — is invisible to the renderer. That's exactly the bug: the HTTP error arrives, `errorMessage` gets set, but nothing tells Angular to look again. Converting both fields to signals in `login.ts` and `register.ts`.

content.text:
Frontend rebuilt with the fix. Since this requires an actual JS engine to observe (curl can't render Angular's client-side reactivity), the verification is for you to do visually — but the fix itself is solid: `errorMessage` and `submitting` are now signals, both `login.ts` and `register.ts` write to them via `.set(...)`, and the templates read them as `errorMessage()`/`submitting()`. Signal writes always schedule change detection in zoneless Angular regardless of whether the write happens inside a synchronous event handler or an async `subscribe()` callback, so the error banner and the button's disabled/label state will now update correctly on a failed login or a duplicate-email registration.

Good catch — that's a real correctness bug that would've silently swallowed every login/register error in the UI.

content.text:
Summary:

- **`backend/src/sources/`**: `types.ts` (the `PollAdapter`/`StreamAdapter` extensibility interface), `rss-adapter.ts` (implements `PollAdapter` via `rss-parser`), `registry.ts` (maps `SourceType` → adapter — adding a websocket source later is just one more entry here).
- **`backend/src/ingestion/`**: `bus.ts` (a plain `EventEmitter` — `newsBus`/`NEWS_CREATED_EVENT` — ready for Phase 4's matching engine to subscribe to), `ingest.ts` (creates the `News` row, relies on the `(sourceId, externalId)` unique constraint to silently no-op on repeat polls, publishes to the bus only for genuinely new items), `scheduler.ts` (loads active sources at startup, polls each immediately then on its own `pollIntervalSeconds`, isolates failures per-source so one bad feed doesn't take down the others).
- **`backend/prisma/seed.ts`** (`npm run seed`): upserts the 3 categories and your 3 RSS sources — this is dev-seed data standing in for admin CRUD, not a replacement for it.

Verified live against the running stack: scheduler logged "3 active source(s)", and all three feeds landed real rows — NYT World (55), MarketWatch (10), FEMA (10), 75 total, matching exactly.

**Still open**: Phase 2 (admin CRUD) doesn't exist yet, so the only way to manage sources right now is the seed script — worth circling back to before this goes further.

  SENT
  FAILED

model Category {

  @@map("sources")
}

}

content.text:
Phase 2 complete:

- **`backend/src/admin/`** — `categories.routes.ts`, `sources.routes.ts`, `users.routes.ts`, full CRUD, all mounted behind `requireAuth + requireRole('ADMIN')` in `admin/index.ts`.
- **Delete guards** (app-level, not silent cascades): a category with existing sources can't be deleted (409), a source with ingested news can't be deleted — deactivate it instead (409); an admin can't delete their own account (400). Subscriptions do cascade-delete with their user/category (harmless, easily re-subscribed); `deliveries.userId`/`categoryId` go to `NULL` on delete instead of vanishing, preserving the audit trail — required a schema migration (`onDelete` rules), now applied.
- **Sources CRUD is wired live into the scheduler** — I refactored `scheduler.ts` to expose `schedulePolling`/`unschedulePolling` keyed by a timer map, so creating, editing, deactivating, or deleting a source through the API takes effect immediately instead of requiring a backend restart (a real gap in the original scheduler design, closed as part of this).
- Added a shared `toPublicUser()` helper (also now used by `/auth/*`) so `passwordHash` never leaks in any response, and a shared `handlePrismaError()` for consistent 400/404/409 mapping across all three route files. Added a JSON error-handling middleware to `index.ts` for anything unexpected.
- Seeded an admin account for testing: **`admin@example.com` / `adminadmin`** (dev-only credentials, obviously rotate before anything resembling production).

Verified live against the running stack: unauthenticated → 401, regular user → 403, admin → full CRUD works, duplicate slug → 409, delete-blocked-by-relation → 409, self-delete → 400, and `passwordHash` confirmed absent from every user response.

**Still open**: no frontend admin UI yet (Phase 6) — everything above is API-only, exercised via curl.

**Still not built**: Phase 4 (matching engine + actual email/Slack delivery) — subscribing doesn't yet *do* anything beyond recording the subscription, since nothing consumes the `news:created` bus event yet.

content.text:
All three fixes verified against the running stack:

1. **Slug auto-generation**: removed the slug input from the category form entirely; it's now computed from the name via a new `slugify()` helper (`frontend/src/app/shared/slugify.ts`) at submit time, for both create and edit.
2. **Webhook-clear bug**: the form was sending `slackWebhookUrl: undefined` when the field was emptied — and `JSON.stringify` drops `undefined` keys entirely, so the backend's `if (slackWebhookUrl !== undefined)` check never saw the change and silently kept the old value forever. Fixed by sending explicit `null` instead, which does survive serialization and correctly clears the column.
3. **Empty CSS files**: deleted 7 empty files (`app.css`, `home.css`, `login.css`, `register.css`, and all three admin-CRUD `.css` files) along with their now-dangling `styleUrl` references in each component — Angular would have failed the build if the file were deleted but still referenced.

Rebuilt and confirmed via the API that a webhook URL set at creation can now be cleared back to `null` through the same edit form.

content.text:
Phase 4 is complete and verified live — the full pipeline now works end-to-end:

- **`backend/src/notifications/`**: `types.ts` (shared `NotificationChannel` interface: `send({ news, destination, categoryName })`), `email-channel.ts`, `slack-channel.ts`, `registry.ts` (mirrors the `sourceAdapters` pattern — `Record<Channel, NotificationChannel>`, so a future SMS/push channel is one more entry).
- **`backend/src/matching/matcher.ts`**: subscribes to the `news:created` bus event, loads active subscriptions for that category, hands off to dispatch.
- **`backend/src/notifications/dispatch.ts`**: emails every subscribed user, broadcasts once to the category's Slack webhook if set, records every attempt in `deliveries` (the `[newsId, channel, userId/categoryId]` unique constraints from Phase 0 now actually do dedup work), and updates `lastEmailSentAt` on successful email sends.
- Had to change `bus.ts` to carry `categoryId` alongside the news row (avoids a redundant DB lookup), and made sure `startMatcher()` runs **before** `startScheduler()` in `index.ts` — a plain `EventEmitter` drops events fired before a listener attaches, so getting that order right mattered.

**One deliberate scope call**: Slack delivery is fully real (an actual `fetch()` POST to the webhook URL). Email delivery is a **console-log stub** — there's no SMTP provider configured, so it logs what it would send rather than pretending to deliver mail nobody asked me to route anywhere. Swapping in real SMTP (nodemailer + env vars) later is a one-file change since everything already goes through the same `NotificationChannel` interface.

**Verified live**: created a duplicate source pointing at the FEMA feed to force 10 genuinely new items, set the Disasters category's Slack webhook to `https://httpbin.org/post`, subscribed a test user — all 10 items produced both an EMAIL delivery (stub-logged) and a real SLACK delivery (HTTP 200 from httpbin), zero failures, `lastEmailSentAt` updated correctly. All test data (source, news, deliveries, user, webhook) cleaned up afterward — the app is back to its normal seeded state.

content.text:
The main page (`http://localhost`) now shows a live latest-news feed:

- **Backend**: `GET /api/news` (public, no auth required) returns the latest news items (default 50, capped at 100), newest first, each with its source and category. Optional `?categoryId=` query param filters to one category — verified both unfiltered (50 items) and filtered (14 Markets-only items, all correctly matching).
- **Frontend**: `Home` now fetches categories + news on load, renders pill-style filter buttons ("All" + one per category) above a list of news items (title linking out, category tag, source name, published date, summary if present). Clicking a filter re-fetches from the backend rather than filtering client-side, so it scales past whatever's currently loaded.

Verified via the live containers — both the unfiltered and category-filtered API responses came back correct, and the page still loads cleanly.
